name: Logvia – Login and Registration with Google Sign-In for WooCommerce
author: Farrukh Sobirov

sections.description:
Logvia replaces the default WordPress and WooCommerce login and registration forms with clean, fast screens that work in any theme.

What you get

  • Popup or slide-in panel with Log in / Sign up tabs. Opens from menu items, any #logvia-login link, a CSS class, the [logvia_link] shortcode, links to the login page, or automatically after a delay.

  • Menu items that change with the visitor: Log in / Sign up for guests, My account / Log out for customers.

  • Login with email or username, “remember me” and errors shown in place, without a page reload.

  • Registration with email verification. Visitors receive a six-digit code. The account is created only after the code is confirmed, so your store fills up with real customers instead of spam accounts.
  • Password reset by link or by six-digit code, on your own branded screen or inside the popup.
  • Continue with Google. Uses Google’s official OAuth flow with PKCE. No extra plugin or SDK needed.
  • WooCommerce My Account login/register is replaced automatically, and new users get the WooCommerce “customer” role.
  • Require an account to check out (optional). Guests fill their cart, log in or register at checkout and come straight back with the cart kept.
  • Works with any theme, classic or block. The screens live on a normal WordPress page, so your header, footer and layout stay in place.
  • Drag & drop form builder with 15 field types: name, phone with country code, country and state, dropdowns, radio buttons, checkbox lists, terms checkbox, dates, numbers and more. Save answers to the profile, WooCommerce billing details or custom fields.
  • Checkout login: the WooCommerce “Returning customer?” box opens the Logvia popup.
  • Bot protection: Cloudflare Turnstile, Google reCAPTCHA v2 and v3, password strength meter and rules, adjustable login lockout.
  • Every text is editable: headings, button labels and field labels on all screens, and the subject and text of every email.
  • Members-only mode: show a popup that cannot be closed until the visitor logs in, on every page or only on the pages you choose.
  • Your colours. Choose an accent colour and a centered or image-split layout. Developers can override every template from their theme.

Built with security in mind

  • Passwords are never stored in plain text, even while the email is being verified.
  • Login, code and email requests are rate limited.
  • Staff accounts (administrators, editors, shop managers) cannot use Google sign-in unless you allow it.
  • Error and success messages are never taken from the URL as text, so nobody can make your site show a fake message.
  • Lost-password requests never reveal whether an account exists.

Shortcodes

  • [logvia] – the full set of screens (used on the account page).
  • [logvia_login], [logvia_register], [logvia_forgot] – a single form anywhere.
  • [logvia_link type="login|register|both|account|logout"] – a link that opens the popup or the account page.

Logvia Pro

Logvia Pro is a separate, optional add-on that adds features which are not part of this plugin: file upload, profile photo, username and account-type fields, manual account approval (B2B and wholesale), “log in to add to cart”, password-less sign-up, and extra fields on My Account and the Users screen. Everything in this plugin works fully without it.

External services

When Google sign-in is enabled and a visitor clicks “Continue with Google”, the plugin connects to Google:

  • The visitor is sent to https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth to choose a Google account.
  • Your server sends the one-time authorization code, your Client ID and Client secret to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token.
  • Your server reads the visitor’s Google account ID, name, email address and whether the email is verified from https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo.

Nothing is sent to Google unless Google sign-in is enabled and the visitor chooses it. Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy apply.

When a captcha is enabled under Settings → Logvia → Security, the forms load the provider’s script and your server checks each answer with the provider, sending the answer token and the visitor’s IP address:

  • Cloudflare Turnstile: https://challenges.cloudflare.com (Terms, Privacy).
  • Google reCAPTCHA: https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ (Terms, Privacy).

Developers

Filters: logvia_messages, logvia_validate_registration, logvia_default_redirect, logvia_login_redirect, logvia_template, logvia_template_args, logvia_hide_page_title, logvia_client_ip, logvia_rate_limits, logvia_text, logvia_field_types, logvia_field_maps, logvia_validate_fields, logvia_meta_key_allowed, logvia_pre_send_email, logvia_email_html, logvia_purchase_requires_login, logvia_google_user_is_privileged.

Actions: logvia_customer_created, logvia_fields_saved.

sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Logvia creates a page called “Account access” at /auth/ with the login, registration and reset screens under it (for example /auth/login/).
  3. Go to Settings → Logvia to choose colours, Google sign-in and WooCommerce options.
  4. Make sure your site can send email (an SMTP plugin is recommended), because verification codes and reset links are sent by email.

Setting up Google sign-in

  1. In Google Cloud Console open APIs & Services → Credentials and create an OAuth client ID of type Web application.
  2. Copy the redirect URL shown on Settings → Logvia → Google sign-in into Authorized redirect URIs.
  3. Paste the Client ID and Client secret into Logvia and enable Google sign-in.
sections.faq:
Does it work without WooCommerce?

Yes. Login, registration, password reset and Google sign-in work on any WordPress site. The WooCommerce options appear when WooCommerce is active.

Can I still use wp-login.php?

Yes. By default wp-login.php keeps working. You can optionally send its visitors to Logvia. If you ever get locked out, add define( 'LOGVIA_DISABLE_WP_LOGIN_REDIRECT', true ); to wp-config.php.

How do I change the design?

Pick an accent colour, corner radius and layout under Settings → Logvia → Appearance. For finer changes, add CSS in Appearance → Customize → Additional CSS (classic themes) or in the Site Editor’s Styles (block themes), for example .logvia { --logvia-radius: 4px; }. To change the markup, copy a file from wp-content/plugins/logvia/templates/ to your-theme/logvia/ and edit it.

The verification email does not arrive

Logvia sends email through WordPress (wp_mail). Many hosts do not deliver it reliably; install an SMTP plugin and send a test email.

Does it work with page caching?

The account page sends no-cache headers and the DONOTCACHEPAGE flag, which most caching plugins respect. If yours does not, exclude /auth/ from the cache.
sections.changelog:
1.3.3

  • New: phone field with round country flags, a searchable country list and the dialling code shown in the field. A pasted “+998 …” number picks the country by itself.
  • New: popup tab colour settings (Settings → Logvia → Appearance).
  • Fix: theme button hover colours no longer show on the popup tabs and buttons.

1.3.2

  • Email texts and members-only mode are now editable in the plugin settings.
  • Removed the custom CSS box; use Additional CSS or the Site Editor instead.

1.3.1

  • First public release.
